item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
1. A larger chunk of writing is not intrinsically bad. In fact, having a larger post to sort of anchor the narrative up to that point is a useful technique.

The issue I have with it is that it's a huge wall of text. The sentence flow isn't great, there's a lot of "it was this, it was that", and it does a great deal of telling rather than showing. The areas where you're supposed to intuit things feels artificial, like you can sense the hand of the author trying to create a creepy situation.

2. The anomaly is too direct in the sense that it's obviously anomalous. If you look at Abwesenheit or Tower-B, you can explain it away. "The diver is lying, he doesn't have any proof." "Hellmuth was just a good director, none of these shots are impossible". The extent to which people are having their accounts hijacked with the spooky messages is a little too hard to deny, especially when they start posting despite being banned.

(And for the record, "they were hacked" is not very believable to me. The attacker would've had to find the posts when they were mentioned, break in to large organizations like Twitter and Archive.org, but only use it for the purposes of changing some creepy text?)

Overall, it feels too much like an electronic anomaly that fucks with the system. Might work in a scip, but it messes with the tone and style of Parawatch.

item.content:encoded:
I don't know if responding to crit comments is in my best interest but I feel like I should voice my disagreements with this.

1. Having long pieces of writing makes total sense considering the circumstances and barely messes with the flow enough to detract from the quality.

2. I don't understand your argument here. You say the anomaly is too in your face, but it's very well balanced considering the format. The pacing leading up to its "attack" on the server is well done, and though we get more info than we usually do in a Parawatch article, it's not like it's ever full on revealed.

I know I didn't write the article but yeah, saw the comment and felt I needed to respond.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There are two main complaints I have regarding this.

Firstly, blanket's post is a huge wall of text which hurts the short, forum exchange flow that had been happening up to that point (discovering that archives were getting messed with, etc.) I get that this is a forum and he's rambling not writing, but this could easily be restructured to fit better within the piece.

Second, the anomaly itself is shown too much. Parawatch is about exploring the more obliquely paranormal, whereas the weird edits on posts is too in-your-face, as well as being a bit of a "generic creepy" thing cliche.

The execution overall really doesn't work for me. -1

All images made by me via inspect element, all usernames changed to ones I made up.
Thanks to Popsioak for helping me with early ideas, and the crit of Henzoid, RadioactiveRads, NatVoltaic, and Westrin.

Spoilers
Spoilers

There was an sentient infohazard within the company servers that grew over time. One day, the night shift tried to destroy the servers out of fear, and instead got absorbed into part of the infohazard, becoming a collective mind. They really don't like being known about, and the last time the farm was mentioned was the post on the sub. Until now, at least.
